title: Cascade refactor log — quick brain-dump
content:
Context:
- Personal brain-dump while walking through the large refactor that touches request routing, KV cache lifecycle, and the batching layer. This is messy notes-to-self + checklist for follow-ups.

Goals for this doc:
- Capture immediate follow-ups I keep thinking of during code read.
- Surface quick tests to validate behavioral invariants.
- Draft rollback / mitigation signals so we can ship with lower risk.

High-level concerns / hypotheses:
1) KV cache warmup: changes to eviction hooks could create longer first-request latencies for long-tail users. Hypothesis: cold sequences will see 20–40% higher latency for first few tokens.
2) Batching boundary shift: moving batching trigger to enqueue-time may reduce tail but could increase head-of-queue starvation for tiny requests.
3) Routing header parity: new header normalization logic might drop tenant-specific route overrides that some internal customers rely on.
4) Metrics fidelity: we removed a counter in router that we used in dashboards; need to re-create or adapt queries.

Quick tests to run locally / in dev cluster (ordered by ease):
- perf/unit: run local perf harness with 2k sequences (len distribution: 8/32/256) and check P50/P95/P99 token latency before/after patch.
- kv-smoke: script to simulate repeated conversations, verify KV hit rate increases over time; assert no negative memory leak after 10k requests.
- enqueue-starve: synthetic load with 50% tiny requests (<=16 tokens) and 50% long; assert tiny P95 does not regress >10%.
- header-roundtrip: curl a request with X-Tenant-Override and ensure routed model matches expected.
- metric-check: run dashboard queries (traceids) to confirm counter re-appears in telemetry.

Instrumentation & observability additions (small, shipable as follow-ups):
- Add "kv_warmup_latency_ms" histogram at eviction boundary.
- Emit an event when batching trigger changes the slot allocation (sampled 1/1000).
- Reintroduce "router.override_applied" counter; backfill explanation in console docs.

Rollback / safety plan (fast path):
- Canary rollout: 5% traffic for 24h, measure three primary signals: user-facing latency (P95 tokens), error-rate (5xxs and internal router errors), and cost (GPU tokens/min).
- Auto-fallback policy: if P95 increases >15% or 5xxs >2x baseline for 30m, route that shard back to previous container image automatically.
- Manual triggers: list of owners to call (pager) and exact deployment IDs.

Owned tickets / TODOs (me / follow-ups):
- TODO-1: Add unit harness for KV eviction edge-case (owner: Juno) — Linear INF-934.
- TODO-2: Small metric shim + dashboard update (owner: Maya).
- TODO-3: Add sampling trace on batching allocation + short doc explaining heuristics (owner: Rohan).
- TODO-4: Run load test across dedicated pool (+ draft results in GH comment).

Open questions / unknowns (need answers before wider rollout):
- Does any internal customer depend on router header normalization? Quick check: search for X-Tenant-Override usage in infra repos and ask SE.
- Are there any downstream jobs that read the old counter semantics? (Likely: billing helpers).
- How will the new batching trigger interact with Dedicated autoscaling buffer? Might need to increase headroom by 10% temporarily.

Quick checklist for the canary day:
- [ ] Bump canary to 5% using rollout pipeline (deploy id: TBD).
- [ ] Enable sampling traces for both old and new flows (trace-sample-rate: 1%).
- [ ] Monitor kv_warmup_latency_ms, router.override_applied, batching.starve_events.
- [ ] Keep a Slack channel open and pinned runbook (link above).
- [ ] If rollback triggers fire, execute automated route swap and postmortem: first 12h summary due.

Notes-to-self: snippets and commands
- Local perf harness: 
  ./scripts/perf_harness --model gpt-lite --seq-distribution 8,32,256 --requests 2000 --concurrency 32
- KV smoke quick: 
  python misc/kv_smoke.py --conversations 200 --turns 20 --warmup 5
- Canary rollout (kubectl snippet): 
  kubectl set image deployment/serving-runtime serving-runtime=ghcr.io/redwood/serving-runtime:canary-20241102 && kubectl rollout status deploy/serving-runtime

Post-canary follow-ups (if green):
- Clean up feature flags and remove old router counter shim (schedule: 2 weeks after full rollout).
- Draft a short "what changed" note for Console team so they can adjust dashboards.

Thoughts about longer-term refactor hygiene:
- We should keep small, focused integration tests that exercise the full path (router -> batching -> runtime -> GPU) in CI but with mocked GPUs to catch contract breaks fast.
- Maintain a dependency map for modules that affect request semantics; auto-generate on PRs that touch more than 2 modules.

Random scribbles / heuristics I keep thinking about:
- For canaries, prefer time-windowed metrics over single spikes; short outages can be noisy.
- If a regression is only visible at P99 and affects <1% of traffic, evaluate whether it's acceptable or needs immediate rollback based on customer SLAs.

If you read this later (future me):
- If anything is unclear, run the header-roundtrip test first — usually surface the biggest customer-impact bug.
- Keep the ticket lean: write the minimal repro steps.

--- end of dump ---
